Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second innings! The Australian players make their way out to the middle. Pakistani bowlers finally get some rest and out comes their openers - Abdullah Shafique and Imam-ul-Haq. Mitchell Starc to steam in with the ball. A couple of slips and gully in place for the right-hander. Time for the first ball, here we go!
... SECOND INNINGS ...

It's been a tough two days for Pakistan. They had to toil hard in the field to grab every wicket. They did come up with certain plans and tactics but not everything went their way. They grabbed an early wicket on Day 3 as well, but Pat Cummins played a fiery cameo and added salt to the wound, and notched up a healthy total. There were 7 bowlers used by Pakistan in this innings and all of them had to work really hard. We can see the pitch is still assisting the batters. Pakistan will be coming to bat high on confidence considering their batting performance in the previous game.

Well, better late than never! Australia have finally declared! They won the toss and batted first and have done justice to that. It's been a scintillating batting performance from the visitors. Usman Khawaja and Steven Smith set the platform for Australia on Day 1 by scoring runs freely. Usman Khawaja carried on and notched up an exceptional 160 and then Alex Carey guided Australia over 500 with his gutsy knock of 93. They were other vital contributions as well, that eventually helped them to put a massive total of 556 on the board. But now it's time for them to come out and bowl. The pitch will be assisting the spinners just a tad, and Swepson and Nathon Lyon will play a key role in helping Australia grab some wickets.

We are ready for live action! The players are out in the middle. There are no signs of declaration as Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins will resume their batting. Shaheen Afridi will begin with the ball. Here we go...

Australia bossed Day 2 as Khawaja stood tall and notched up a brilliant 160. There were a few other contributions as well but Carey's knock was the most significant one. That helped Australia breach the 500-run mark. Pakistani players will be pretty tired having fielded for 180 overs over the last 2 days. They would want to quickly wrap up things in the first session itself and come out to bat. Australia would look to add as many as they can or it could be a declaration as well. We will have to wait and see. All eyes will be on Mitchell Swepson as well who is making his long-awaited Test debut. The pitch will surely help the spinners as there are a few footmarks created, the ball is turning and is keeping low on odd balls as well. What will the pitch have in store for us? For that, you will have to stay tuned, enjoy the coverage and see how Day 3 pans out.

Hello and a warm welcome to the second Test of the three-match Test series between Pakistan and Australia. We are heading towards Day 3 now which is also called the moving day but by the looks of it, the game is only 'moving' in one direction which is another stalemate. Too early to say though as Australia's bowling is still left. We can only hope that we get a result out of this and there is some excitement for the fans.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then. That concludes the proceedings for the second day of the second Test. Australia are in a commanding position with 505 on the board. One suspects that we shall NOT see any overnight declaration, as Cummins would not want to give the Pakistan batters any mental relaxation. Runs are not an issue and with no known batter at the crease, Australia might want to bat for around 30 minutes and then declare, just to irritate the opposition openers and not give them any time to change over. All the same, there is an equal probability of Australia getting bowled out too. The action will continue on 14th March with the first ball at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT). See you then, cheers!

Alex Carey is in for a chat. He says it is great to have 500 runs on the board and not getting to the three-digit figure does not hurt him much. Hopes that the wicket starts deteriorating. Adds, it has been fabulous coming down to Pakistan. Praises the hospitality and the food in the country. On being asked about learning some Urdu, Carey shakes his head with a laugh.

The pitch did offer some turn and swing later in the day, but Pakistan bowlers managed to grab just one wicket in the final session. The hosts did manage to grab 3 wickets in the second session and they would have thought of wrapping things up quickly, however, Australia had other plans. They did take the new ball as well but could not trouble the Australian batters much with it. However, Babar Azam did manage to grab the wicket of Alex Carey, but it was a little too late for them. It's been tough for Pakistan, they have bowled over 180 overs in the last two days! However, they will be high on confidence once they come to bat, considering their batting performance in the previous game. Although it is going to be a challenge since the pitch will be assisting the spinners more.

The story remains to be the same! Australia continued to score runs freely, while Pakistan had to toil hard in the field. Another day in this Test that has belonged to the visitors, as they have managed to put a healthy total on the board and ended Day 2 in a commanding position. Alex Carey and Mitchell Starc put together 98 runs and guided Australia over 500 runs. Alex Carey missed out on a well-deserved century by just 7 runs, but he should be proud of the way he has played today. Australia have enough runs on the board and they will be looking to declare and grab some early wickets in the morning of Day 3.

Australia lost two early wickets early in the session. But after losing Usman Khawaja for a mighty 160, and Travis Head. Cameron Green and Alex Carey stitched together 45 runs and helped Australia cross the 400-run mark. However, Cameron Green could not carry on till the end of the session and he perished just before the Tea break. Austalia are still building but are in a comfortable position. Every run from here will hurt Pakistan as Australia have already notched up a healthy total. A thrilling final session awaits. Do join us back at 3:30 pm IST (10:00 am GMT).

An entertaining second session! 29 overs, 75 runs, and 3 wickets in this session. Pakistan will certainly go into the Tea break as the happier side. They have managed to grab three vital wickets in this session. Sajid Khan displayed his magic and grabbed the wicket of Travis Head and the big fish, Usman Khawaja with a classical off-spinner. Nauman Ali followed up with another beauty to dismiss Cameron Green at the stroke of Tea. The pitch has started offering some assistance to the spinners, and the seamers as well are getting some swing off this surface. Pakistan will be hoping they can wrap the Australian innings in the third session.

Not much on offer! Pakistan bowlers did not get much purchase of the deck and could not get the new ball to do its magic. Although once Faheem Ashraf got in his rhythm. Pakistan bowlers have their task cut out and would be interesting to see how they go about with the second session. Do join us at 1310 IST (0740 GMT) to find out how things pan out.

The night watchman shines in the morning session! Nathan Lyon made the most of his reprieve and racked up a 54-run stand with Khawaja, where he was the aggressor. Eventually, Faheem Ashraf came up with a peach to get rid of Lyon. Later, Khawaja and Head batted sensibly, did well to put away the bad balls and made sure Australia do not lose any more wickets till Lunch. Also, Khawaja became only the third opening batsman to score 150 against Pakistan. The visitors look to be on track to reach the 450-run mark.

Usman Khawaja was the stand-out player for Australia, he scored an unbeaten 127 and guided his side to a total of 251 at the end of Day 1. The visitors will be hoping they can get over 400 runs which will not be a challenge as the pitch is assisting the batters. While Pakistan will be hoping they can cause some early trouble with the second new ball which is just 10 overs old. The pitch is good for batting but as predicted earlier on, it will be getting better for the spinners, and Sajid Khan and Nauman Ali will have to put their best foot forward. Will Australia go on to score big? Or will Pakistan grab some early wickets? We will find out. Stay tuned!

Welcome back, folks! We are now into Day 2 of this exciting Test between Australia and Pakistan. We witnessed an intriguing first day of this Test with Australia ending the day in a commanding position. The hosts might be on the back foot but they will be coming into Day 2 hoping they can grab some early wickets and take things under control. Although it’s not going to be an easy task considering the batting depth of Australia. Another thrilling day of Test awaits us.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

That concludes the proceedings for the first day of the second Test. It's been a great day for Australia and the day certainly belonged to one man, Usman Khawaja, he will look to replicate the same on Day 2 as well. The first ball of Day 2 will be at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) but as usual, our build-up will begin in advance. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Usman Khawaja is down for a chat. He says that he had a great partnership with Smith and there's still a lot of batting to come. Tells that the wicket looks good to bat on and it seems like it is going to stay this way for the first 2 or 3 days. Mentions that the ball had started reversing well in the second session so they had to get defensive with their approach. Adds that once again in the final session, they started bowling negative lines to dry up the scoring rate. States that everyone in his family except him was born in Karachi so it means a lot for him to get a hundred here.

The hosts will be disappointed with their bowling performance, but they will be satisfied after grabbing the big wicket of Steven Smith. They had to toil hard for the wicket but they were rewarded at the end. Pakistan came out with a different plan in the final session, Sajid Khan and Nauman Ali both were bowling negative lines and were not allowing the batters to score freely. We did notice the pacers get some reverse-swing at the end of the second session, however, they were not used much in the first hour of the final session. They took the second new ball immediately and were rewarded with the wicket of Steven Smith with it. However, they have to work a lot harder to grab early wickets in the first session of Day 2, and not let Australia get away with a big total.

Australia have scored 251 runs at the loss of three wickets. It's safe to say that Day 1 of this Test match has belonged to the visitors. However, they will be disappointed after losing Steven Smith at the stroke of Stumps. Khawaja and Smith put on a great show today. They fought hard, showed great resilience and patience against all the negative lines by the Pakistan bowlers, but failed to survive till the end of the day. The duo put together 159 runs and have put Australia in the driver's seat. After missing out on his century in the first Test, Usman Khawaja made sure he gets it this time and brought his 11th Test ton, while Steven Smith, who was looking rock solid in the middle, missed out on his century once again. Australia have plenty of batting to come, and they will be hoping they get to at least 400 from here.

A wicket in the penultimate over of Stumps and a dropped catch on the last ball. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1!

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Session Summary - 27 overs, 72 runs, 0 wickets. Australia bag this session quite comfortably. They headed into the Lunch break with a double blow but after that, both, Khawaja and Smith have countered this session superbly especially with the spinners getting some sharp turn on the odd balls. Runs were coming easily for them and both the batters have done well here to remain unscathed. The consistency in line and lengths was missing from the Pakistani bowlers and the Australian batters took advantage of that although they did pull back things nicely towards the end but could not produce a wicket. With the pitch looking easy for the batters, Khawaja and Smith would look to continue their batting the same way they did in this session and bring their personal milestones while Pakistan bowlers need to come up with a plan to break this partnership soon. Don't take your eyes off folks! There's a brilliant battle between bat and ball going on with Pakistani pacers finding reverse swing. Do join us for the final session which will begin at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT).

The visitors started off well and both the openers looked solid in the middle. They were troubled by the bowlers a tad at the beginning with the new red cherry, but they did well to survive and started scoring freely. However, that did not last for too long. David Warner perished after his gusty knock of 36 and soon the No. 1 Test batter, Marnus Labuschagne was dismissed for 0 after facing 9 balls. Australia were 79 for no loss in the first 17 overs, they have managed to score just 21 more runs in the next 10 overs and lost two vital wickets. Usman Khawaja has looked rock solid for now, he brought up yet another half-ton and will be looking to carry on the same way in the next session, along with Steven Smith at the other end. Will Pakistan be able to break the current partnership? Or will Australia continue to score without any damage? We will find out in the next session which begins at 1:10 pm IST (7:40 am GMT). Stay tuned!

An intriguing first session of this Test match! The session will certainly be shared by the two sides. Australia were cruising along nicely in the first hour, but Pakistan fought back and grabbed two big wickets. First, it was David Warner who was sent back to the hut by Faheem Ashraf by a peach of a delivery, and then a direct hit by Sajid Khan saw Marnus Labuschagne walk back without scoring. Well, we don't see that happening too often, do we? Pakistan will be pleased with their bowling show so far, they have fought back well but they have a lot more to do now.

OUT! RUN OUT! Needless from Australia and Pakistan will be on cloud 9 seeing the back of Marnus Labuschagne. Nauman Ali bowls a flatter delivery, on middle. Marnus Labuschagne leans and drives it to mid off. He sets off for a quick single. Sajid Khan has three stumps to aim at and he does so by collecting it with his right hand quickly and hitting the bullseye. Pakistan are already celebrating but the umpire takes it upstairs to confirm. Replay shows that Marnus Labuschagne is caught short of his crease. He walks back with disappointment on his face. He goes for 0 and what a big moment in the game.
Is that a run out? There is a direct throw at the bowler's end. Marnus Labuschagne looks in trouble. Yes, he falls just short of his ground. He walks back!

TOSS - Australia have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.

Pakistan would be happy with the draw in the first Test but they would also be looking for a win in this match with crucial WTC points at stake. Their batters are in excellent form and will look to carry forward their confidence on this lively track. Their batting is further bolstered by the return of Faheem Ashraf who missed the first Test due to Covid-19. Hasan Ali also is likely to replace Naseem Shah. Pakistan have generally been very dominant at home in Tests and if they win this Test, it will be their tenth consecutive home Test without facing a defeat since losing to South Africa in 2007. Both teams will head into this Test with the series still locked at 0-0 and have everything to play for. Will Australia get their first win at Karachi? Will Pakistan maintain their home run? Will this Test produce a result? All the answers will become clear soon. First, let's see how Day 1 pans out. Toss and team news in a bit.

Australia have interestingly never won a Test at the National Stadium,‌ Karachi. They would be looking to break that stat and also gain some crucial Worst Test Championship points. They are playing at Karachi after 24 years and after ending the first Test in a draw, they would be certainly be eager to get a win here. With the spinners getting some help on this pitch, Australia have announced that Mitchell Swepson will be making his long-awaited Test debut and will replace Josh Hazlewood. The Queenslander will be the first frontline leg-spinner to debut for Australia in Tests since Bryce McGain in 2009.

Pakistan and Australia are set to lock horns in this second Test of the three-match Test series here at Karachi. The opening Test at Rawalpindi ended in a draw where the nature of the pitch drew a lot of criticism as 1187 runs were scored over the course of five days and only 14 wickets fell. The game progressed at a snail's pace but the Karachi pitch is said to be spin-friendly and thus, the chances of producing a result on this pitch are more likely. That shall also keep the fans excited as well as the series exciting. With this series seen as historic, let's hope this Test is full of action and forces all of us glued to the television. On that note, welcome to the coverage.
